messages.subject_clean: Should mgcv be in Imports: rather than just Suggests: ?
messages.body_plain:
I have a package that Suggests: ggplot2 for a vignette. I got an email from Prof. Ripley notifying me that my package is currently failing R CMD check because of an unstated dependency on mgcv:

>  Quitting from lines 437-441 (companion-to-sample-file-1314.Rmd)
>    Error: processing vignette 'companion-to-sample-file-1314.Rmd' failed with diagnostics:
>   there is no package called 'mgcv'
(https://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_results_grattan.html)

The failure occurs because I use `geom_smooth()` which in that context invokes mgcv, but mgcv is not listed in Imports: so CRAN does not install it when it installs ggplot2. I know I can just put mgcv in Suggests, but I wonder whether the problem might be with ggplot2.

(Asking here, not on GitHub, because it's a question.)

You will need to coerce your data into a "spatial" kind, as implemented in `sp` or as of late, `sf` packages. You might want to give the vignettes a whirl before you proceed.
Roughly, you will have to coerce the data to Spatial* (you could go for a point, raster or grid type, I think) and also specify the projection. Once you have that, plotting should be handled by packages.

https://cran.r-project.org/web/views/Spatial.html
http://www.datacarpentry.org/R-spatial-raster-vector-lesson/10-vector-csv-to-shapefile-in-r/

Cheers,
Roman

require(splines)
require(ggplot2)

set.seed(12345)
dat = data.frame(claim=rbinom(1000,1,0.5))
mns = c(3.4,3.6)
sds = c(0.24, 0.35)
dat$wind = exp(rnorm(nrow(dat), mean=mns[dat$claim+1], sd=sds[dat$claim+1]))
dat = dat[order(dat$wind),]

ggplot(dat, aes(wind,claim))+geom_point()+
  geom_smooth(method = "glm",

              formula = y ~ splines::ns(x, df=5))+

Lily,

Here is a nice blog post about using the different devices with special fonts. But using your millipercent symbol isn't so bad.

library(tidyverse)

pdf("test.pdf")
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = wt)) + geom_point() + labs(x= "blah‰", y = "blah2‰")
dev.off()

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = wt)) + geom_point() + labs(x= "blah‰", y = "blah2‰")

ggsave(filename = "cairo.pdf", device = cairo_pdf)
ggsave(filename = "normal.pdf")
ggsave("png.png")

yields the attached pdfs and png.

The normal pdf does what you say, but both the png and the cairo pdf does what you want.

I am on a mac so this is expected behavior. If you are on windows or linux you might need further guidance.

If you run the previous, what do you get? Where are you struggling?

Brandon
